newsitem.title: USA: Coke Enterprises buys two bottlers for $1.66 billion.
newsitem.headline: Coke Enterprises buys two bottlers for $1.66 billion.

text.p: Coca-Cola Enterprises Inc. said Tuesday it planned to buy two major North American Coke bottlers, Coca-Cola Beverages Ltd. of Canada and Coca-Cola Bottling Co. of New York Inc., for about $1.66 billion.
Under an agreement in principle, the giant Coke bottler said it would buy ownership stakes in the two bottlers currently held by Coca-Cola Co.

Coca-Cola, which owns 45 percent of Coke Enterprises, also has a 48 percent stake in Coke Canada and a 49 percent interest in Coke New York. Analysts estimated the sale of those two investment stakes to Coke Enterprises to be worth around $500 million.
Coke Enterprises said it also intended to buy the rest of the two companies from the remaining owners.

"With this transaction, Coca-Cola Enterprises will now represent more than 65 percent of the Coca-Cola Co.'s North American bottle and can volume, and about 20 percent of the Coca-Cola Co.'s worlwide volume," Coke Enterprises Chief Executive Summerfield Johnston said.

The world's largest bottler of non-alcoholic beverages, with $10.3 billion in revenues last year, Coke Enterprises said its aim would be to expand the share of Coke products in both markets by reorganizing the two operations to meet its decentralized management approach.

"Our interest in this transaction is based on the significant volume growth and margin improvement opportunities we see in the Canadian and New York markets," Coke Enterprises President Henry Schimberg said.

The New York and Canadian markets together encompass 51 million consumers whose per capita consumption rate of Coke products falls below the level maintained in U.S. markets controlled by Coke Enterprises.

The deal would give the Atlanta-based bottling giant its first foray into Canada. Earlier this year, Coke Enterprises entered Britain with its $2 billion purchase of Coca-Cola and Cadbury Schweppes bottling operations. The company last year also expanded into Belgium and France through similar purchases.
Wall Street analysts said the deal would allow Coke Enterprises to approach the United States and Canada as a single North American marketplace.

"It's going to take a while for them to get their act together," said Roy Burry, at Oppenheimer & Co. "They have to make the necessary restructuring moves to integrate the U.S. and Canadian businesses ... We're talking one to two years there. I would guess that subsequent to that time, you would begin to see an increase in per capita consumption."

Coke Enterprises said it would pay C$17, or about $12.25, for each of the 19.6 million shares of the Canadian Coke bottler held by Coca-Cola Co. It also plans to make an offer for approximately 52 percent of Coke Canada held by the public at C$19.50, or $14, a share in cash, a price representing a premium of about 20 percent over the average closing price of Coke Canada's shares for the last four weeks.

In January 1994, Coca-Cola Enterprises bought 4 percent of Coke New York from Coca-Cola Co., along with a five-year right of first refusal on Coke's remaining 49 percent investment in Coke New York and an option to negotiate for this ownership interest after two years.
It said it intends to acquire the remaining 47 percent of Coke New York currently held by private investors.
The company expected to complete the deals by the end of September.
Coca-Cola Beverages Ltd. operates in all 10 Canadian provinces, reaching a population of 27 million people, and represents 95 percent of The Coca-Cola Co.'s unit case volume in Canada.
Based on current currency exchange rates, Coke Canada generated 1996 net operating revenues of approximately $690 million on 259 million unit cases.

The Coca-Cola Bottling Co. of New York Inc. operates in the New York metropolitan area, certain other areas in the state of New York, and in parts of Connecticut, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New Jersey, and Vermont, serving a population of 24 million.
Coke New York sold 214 million unit cases in 1996, producing net operating revenues of about $744 million.
